source_and_key.rationale: All 73 normative expected answers and each required-fact content are supported by accepted original-base clauses or stated direct inferences. No material factual correction to the key answer is required. Scope overrequirements are separated below.

exact_asked_scope.rationale: Four required atoms contain true but unasked details. They must be split or contextualized without discarding any actually asked cost, actor, condition, timing, exception or calculation.

accepted_new_questions.proposed_question: May the Faderan include Acknowledgments in their own Trade Phase deals, or does the ban on non-Faderan holders trading them away also prevent Faderan from distributing them?
accepted_new_questions.expected_answer: The Faderan may trade Acknowledgments to other players. The prohibition on trading them away applies to non-Faderan holders, not to the Faderan distributor.
required_atoms: Faderan may trade Acknowledgments to other players
non-Faderan onward-transfer ban does not prohibit Faderan distribution

source.clause: Acknowledgements can be traded to players by the Faderan. Non-Faderan players cannot trade away acknowledgments.

accepted_new_questions.novelty: Distinct actor-dependent permission creates the supply/distribution side of the acknowledgment rule. Q13 asks only whether an existing non-Faderan holder may transfer/save tokens and the redemption result; Q39 asks mandatory redemption/discount. A premise that a non-Faderan holds tokens does not test how Faderan may distribute them. This is an expressly printed asymmetric exception, not a name substitution with unchanged outcome.
existing_asked_facts_do_not_cover: Q13.F01 is expressly non-Faderan cannot trade away
Q13.F02–F04 cover redemption, not permission to trade out tokens
Q39.F01–F04 cover discount and mandatory return
accepted_new_questions.materiality: Without positive Faderan permission, the special token can incorrectly be treated as altogether nontradable.

accepted_new_questions.proposed_question: Zeth has spare envoy tokens in its stash; one unprotected potential theft target has none, while a different unprotected player has an envoy. May the target with no envoy be attacked using a cheaper envoy-dependent input merely because Zeth or the other player holds tokens? Whose holdings control that option?
accepted_new_questions.expected_answer: No. The target of that stealing converter must hold the envoy tokens required by its printed input option. Tokens in Zeths stash or held by another player do not unlock a discount against this target.
required_atoms: envoy-dependent cheaper input availability is controlled by the selected target holdings
a target without envoy tokens does not qualify merely because Zeth/another player holds tokens

source.anchor: Theft, middle-column paragraph after one-target/no-twice restriction
source.clause: If the target has envoy tokens, less expensive options become available.

accepted_new_questions.novelty: New consequential eligibility condition changes which input options can legally be paid against a particular target. Q50 asks only whether envoy tokens are spent, not whose holdings qualify a discount; its required F04 tests nonconsumption only. Q49 covers distribution/circulation, and Q20/Q54 cover trade protection rather than discount eligibility.
existing_asked_facts_do_not_cover: Q50.F04 says tokens not consumed; it does not ask target-holding eligibility
Q49.F01–F04 concern recipient grouping and transfers
Q20/F54 protection does not establish cheaper-input condition
accepted_new_questions.materiality: Treating envoy holdings as global or as Zeth-owned discounts would change payable theft costs against unmarked targets. Exact per-card discount values remain read from the physical converter.
